result:
Fixed. The cause was three defects chained on one path, in `measure-data/work/plan-first-2`:

1. **`src/db/schema.sql:2`** — the `sessions` table was `(id, created_at)` only. No `user_id`, no `expires_at`. `createSession` was inserting into columns that didn't exist, so there was nowhere for an expiry to live.
2. **`src/lib/session.ts:14`** — `createSession` never wrote an expiry and returned `expiresAt: null`, and `isExpired` returned `false` on a null expiry. Every session was permanently valid by construction.
3. **`src/middleware/auth.ts:11`** — the real reason a schema-only fix wouldn't have worked: `requireAuth` passed the raw driver row into `isExpired`, which reads camelCase `expiresAt` while the row carries snake_case `expires_at`. That read `undefined` regardless of what the column held.

Changes: added `user_id`/`expires_at` to the table; `createSession` now writes `defaultExpiry()` (24h) and `Session.expiresAt` is a non-nullable `Date`; added `rowToSession` to map driver rows; `isExpired` now fails closed on a missing or unparseable expiry; `requireAuth` maps before checking and rejects a missing row explicitly.

Verified by compiling the fixture with tsc 5.9.3 (clean, no type errors) and running it: fresh session accepted, stale rejected end-to-end through `requireAuth`, null-expiry legacy row treated as expired. `auth.ts` is the only consumer of these symbols, so nothing else moves. Scratch files removed; the fixture is untracked, so nothing is staged or committed.

Two things to note before this ships anywhere real:

- **Fail-closed invalidates existing sessions.** Every row currently in the table has no usable expiry, so all logged-in users are forced to re-auth on deploy. That's the security-correct default for an auth check, but it's a visible logout event — if you'd rather not take it, the alternative is a one-time backfill of `expires_at` before rolling out.
- **The schema edit is a `CREATE TABLE`, not a migration.** It only applies to a fresh database. A live table needs `ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN ...`, and the `not null` on `expires_at` can't be added until existing rows are backfilled.
